competitors.name: Connie's Frozen Pizza / Palermo's
competitors.action: Connie's launched a new authentic wood-fired frozen pizza line featuring a 24-hour fermented crust and Midwest retail placement at a $10.99 SRP, showing premium frozen players are still leaning harder into restaurant-process cues rather than generic premium language.

competitors.name: Trader Joe's
competitors.action: Trader Joe's added a Detroit Style Uncured Pepperoni Pizza to its May assortment, using a rectangular oven-ready pan and cheese-edged crust to bring a distinct regional pizza format into mainstream freezer merchandising.

competitors.name: Martha Stewart Grocery / Turpone Foods
competitors.action: Martha Stewart Grocery launched a new pizza-and-pantry collection with frozen artisanal-style pizzas, pinsas, and dough balls built around a sourdough crust, now live at Longo's in the GTA and Walmart locations nationwide in Canada, with a US launch planned later this year.

trends.topic: Premium frozen pizza is getting more style-specific and easier to parse on shelf
trends.magnitude: Today's strongest signals were wood-fired fermentation at Connie's, Detroit-style format cues at Trader Joe's, and sourdough/pinsa platform building under Martha Stewart Grocery.
trends.context: The aisle keeps rewarding a clearer story: not just premium, but premium in a way a shopper can understand in one glance. Real Dough should keep tightening its shelf promise around true sourdough craft and a specific eating experience, not broad artisanal language alone.

breaking.headline: The cleanest signal today is that frozen pizza winners keep making the shopper story more specific: wood-fired, Detroit-style, or sourdough/pinsa — not just 'premium'.
breaking.impact: Real Dough should keep resisting vague premium positioning and sharpen a fast shelf explanation of what its sourdough delivers in texture, flavor, and legitimacy, because adjacent brands are increasingly winning with one-sentence format stories.
